economics.title: Simultaneous Demand and Supply Shifts
economics.context: Analyze how concurrent shifts in demand and supply affect equilibrium price and quantity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The net effect on equilibrium price depends on the relative size of demand and supply shifts.
Graphical analysis compares new intersection points to identify changed equilibrium outcomes.
If demand shifts right while supply shifts left, equilibrium price is likely to rise.
If demand shifts right and supply shifts right together, equilibrium quantity rises.
Supply and demand shifts can occur together after a natural disaster disrupts production and tastes.
tactical_explanations:
When demand and supply both move, equilibrium price is not pinned by either shift alone.

A large rightward demand shift tends to raise price; a large rightward supply shift tends to lower it. The net price change is the sum of those opposing or reinforcing pressures, so relative magnitudes decide whether the new intersection sits higher, lower, or roughly unchanged. Quantity can also move in either direction depending on which curve travels farther. Simultaneous-shift analysis therefore always asks which force dominates on price and which on quantity.

So the statement is True.

Diagrams compare the old intersection with the new one after both curves move.

Reading the new crossing point against the old one shows whether equilibrium price and quantity rose, fell, or stayed ambiguous.

So the statement is True.

Demand shifting right raises willingness to pay; supply shifting left cuts available output at each price.

Both forces push the intersection upward on the price axis, so equilibrium price is likely to rise even if the quantity change remains ambiguous without sizes.

So the statement is True.

Rightward demand and rightward supply both increase the quantity that clears at the new intersection.

Buyers want more at each price and sellers offer more at each price, so the equilibrium quantity almost always expands. Price may rise or fall depending on which shift is larger, but the quantity conclusion is firm when both curves move right. Natural examples include a tourism boom that lifts demand while new capacity comes online on the supply side.

So the statement is True.

A disaster can destroy plant (supply left) while also changing what households urgently buy (demand shifts).

Both schedules can therefore move in the same episode, not only one at a time.

So the statement is True.

economics.title: Micro turnover edge case
economics.context: Consider a neighbourhood bakery, which has six staff and €2.1m turnover. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Turnover above €10m can push a firm out of the small category even when staff remain below fifty.
Micro status allows either turnover up to €2m or a balance sheet total up to €2m alongside the staff limit.
Exceeding the €2m turnover cap can disqualify a firm from micro status even when staff are below ten.
Small status also requires turnover not exceeding €10m.
A small enterprise may employ fewer than fifty people under EU definitions.
tactical_explanations:
A firm can stay under fifty staff and still leave the small category if turnover rises above €10m. The financial breach alone is enough to push it out.

So the statement is True.

Micro status pairs fewer than ten staff with a financial OR: turnover up to €2m or a balance sheet total up to €2m. Passing one of those financial caps alongside the staff limit can keep the firm micro.

The bakery with six staff and €2.1m turnover may still qualify if its balance sheet stays within €2m. That OR structure is what the statement records.

So the statement is True.

Even with fewer than ten employees, turnover above €2m can remove micro status when the balance sheet also fails its €2m cap. Crossing the turnover ceiling is a real disqualification path.

So the statement is True.

Small status requires turnover not exceeding €10m (or the parallel balance-sheet route) together with the staff limit. The €10m turnover ceiling is part of that package.

So the statement is True.

EU small-enterprise rules allow fewer than fifty people on the payroll. That staff band is the employment side of the official small definition.

So the statement is True.

economics.title: Limited Partnership Structure
economics.context: Review the structure of a limited partnership that combines managing partners with at least one non-managing capital provider. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Terms of the partnership and other operational details may appear alongside profit division in the partnership agreement.
Partners who intend to be equally involved in management and share financial risk often choose a general partnership structure.
Rights and responsibilities of each partner are among the matters settled in the partnership agreement.
Oral promises between founders eliminate the need to settle profit division in a written partnership agreement.
Under unlimited liability a creditor must collect an equal fraction of the debt from every partner simultaneously.
tactical_explanations:
Operational terms can sit beside profit division in the same partnership agreement. Hours, roles, and procedures are common extras beyond the money split.

So the statement is True.

Founders who want equal management involvement and shared financial risk often choose a general partnership structure rather than a limited one.

So the statement is True.

Rights and responsibilities of each partner belong in the agreement alongside ownership percentages. Clear allocation of duties reduces later conflict over who must do what.

Settling those matters in writing is part of forming a workable partnership. The statement correctly includes rights and responsibilities among the agreement's contents.

So the statement is True.

Oral promises leave profit division hard to prove when trust frays. A written partnership agreement remains the proper place to settle how returns are shared, even among friends.

So the statement is False.

Creditors need not collect equal fractions from every partner at once. One general partner can be pursued for the full debt under unlimited liability rules.

So the statement is False.

economics.title: Engineering Firm Share Price Rally
economics.context: Consider an engineering firm whose shares rallied after a contract win, though the firm issued no new equity during the rally. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The contract win obliged the firm to register the rally amount as new share capital on its books.
Expectations of higher future profits from the contract can increase demand and push up share prices.
Shareholders holding stock during the rally may benefit from capital growth if they later sell at higher prices.
The corporation receives the full trading profit whenever existing shareholders sell to new buyers on the exchange.
Rising prices after issue force the board to pay immediate dividends equal to the price increase.
tactical_explanations:
The contract win did not oblige the engineering firm to register the rally amount as new share capital on its books; secondary price moves are not automatic equity subscriptions.

So the statement is False.

Expectations of higher future profits from the contract can increase demand for the stock and push exchange prices up as investors reprice the earnings outlook.

So the statement is True.

Shareholders holding stock during the rally may benefit from capital growth if they later sell at higher prices than they paid for the shares.

Nothing in the rally forces an immediate cash distribution from the board. The investor benefit arrives if and when the holder sells into the higher quote or marks a higher valuation.

So the statement is True.

The corporation does not receive the full trading profit whenever existing shareholders sell to new buyers on the exchange; those gains stay with the selling investors.

So the statement is False.

Rising prices after issue do not force the board to pay immediate dividends equal to the full price increase recorded on the secondary market.

So the statement is False.

economics.title: Price Skimming on New Products
economics.context: Analyze psychological pricing such as charm prices that influence customer perceptions. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production costs when setting the selling price of a product.
Selling only through the firm's own shops is classified as direct distribution rather than indirect distribution in the marketing-mix framework.
Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler is classified as indirect distribution rather than direct distribution in the marketing-mix framework.
Television commercials communicating product benefits is classified as advertising rather than place in the marketing-mix framework.
Penetration pricing sets a relatively low price to gain market share quickly after launch.
tactical_explanations:
Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production costs to set the selling price. Cost base plus margin is the cost-plus rule the statement states.

So the statement is True.

Selling only through the firm's own shops is direct distribution because no independent intermediary sits between producer and buyer. Own-shop paths illustrate that direct place choice.

So the statement is True.

Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler is indirect distribution: the wholesaler is an intermediary on the path to retail. Direct would skip that middle step.

So the statement is True.

Television commercials that communicate product benefits are advertising under promotion, not place decisions about physical access. Ads persuade and inform; warehouses and aisles handle availability. Mixing the commercial with place would confuse message tools with channel tools. Media spend belongs in the promotion toolkit. The statement's advertising classification is therefore right.

So the statement is True.

Penetration pricing sets a relatively low price to gain market share quickly after launch. Fast volume through a low entry price is the penetration aim.

So the statement is True.
